Stated Claim / Post Context:
Swedish Gripen authorised to shoot down Russian missile over Poland but unable to identify it

The pilot of a Swedish Gripen fighter jet patrolling Polish airspace during airspace violations on Friday 20 November was authorised to shoot down a Russian missile but was unable to do so due to difficult weather conditions.

Actual Article Body:
Долучайтеся до клубу УП!

The pilot of a Swedish Gripen fighter jet patrolling Polish airspace during airspace violations on Friday 20 November was authorised to shoot down a Russian missile but was unable to do so due to difficult weather conditions.

Source: General Ireneusz Nowak, Operational Commander of the Polish Armed Forces, in a comment to Rzeczpospolita, as reported by European Pravda

Details: A pair of Swedish Gripen fighter jets were operating under the command of NATO's Combined Air Operations Centre (CAOC) in Uedem, Germany, which is responsible for air operations in this part of Europe. It was the CAOC that issued a so-called condition-based order, authorising pilots to make their own decisions on whether to shoot down an object.

One of the Swedish pilots attempted to intercept an object preliminarily identified as a Russian Kh-101 cruise missile. However, he was unable to identify it either visually or using the aircraft's onboard electro-optical systems.

General Ireneusz Nowak explained that extremely difficult weather conditions in the interception area had prevented the pilot from identifying the target. As a result, despite having NATO authorisation to use weapons, the pilot did not shoot it down.

On Friday 20 November, the military tracked 11 objects that could have posed a threat to Polish airspace. Three of them crossed the border, but none caused any casualties.
